page: Microsoft Azure EC8ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It delivers 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a dedicated 322 GB local solid-state drive (SSD) for temporary storage. The CPU configuration features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, as well as cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced overall compute capacity alongside solid single-thread throughput. In synthetic processor stress testing, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 3022.86, placing it in the top 25 percent of comparable servers, whereas multi-core stress-ng reached 12056.83 in the median tier. Geekbench testing mirrors this trend, producing a single-core score of 1937.0, a multi-core score of 7291.0, and a strong text processing score of 2526.0. In memory and database workloads, the system sustained 10.34 million Redis SET operations per second and registered a PassMark database score of 3718.39, reflecting stable throughput under I/O and caching stress.

With 8 GB of memory per vCPU and fast bundled local SSD storage, the instance exhibits a cost-efficient footprint for memory-dense and latency-sensitive deployments. The trade-off centers on its 4 physical core constraint, which moderates extreme parallel compute throughput relative to compute-focused families. The EC8ads_v6 is technically suited for medium-sized relational databases, in-memory caching systems, search indexing, ETL operations, and enterprise business applications requiring consistent memory overhead.
description: Microsoft Azure EC8ads_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, a 1:8 core-to-memory allocation, and 322 GB of local SSD temporary storage, the instance provides high memory density without hardware GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread execution, highlighted by a top-tier stress-ng single-core rating of 3022.86 and 2526.0 in Geekbench text processing, alongside median multi-core results such as a PassMark CPU score of 14089.21. In-memory data handling is verified by 10.34 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark memory score of 2421.97. The instance delivers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy configurations, making it suited for relational databases, Redis or Memcached clusters, ETL pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise web services.
